ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, an equilateral triangle $ADE$ is constructed on the exterior side of square $ABCD$. What is the measure of $\angle AEB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Let an equilateral triangle $\triangle ADE$ be constructed on the exterior of square ABCD.\\
Therefore, $AB=AD$, $AD=AE$, $\angle BAD=90^\circ$, $\angle DAE=60^\circ$,\\
Thus, $AB=AE$, $\angle BAE=150^\circ$,\\
Hence, $\angle ABE=\angle AEB=\boxed{15^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is square ABCD, A is at the upper right, B is at the upper left, C is at the lower left, and D is at the lower right. With the right side AD of the square as a side, construct outward an equilateral triangle ADE, point E is on the right side of AD, and BE is connected in the figure; what is required is the angle between EA and EB at point E, ∠AEB. Then reason: Because ABCD is a square, AB=AD, and ∠BAD=90°. Because ADE is an equilateral triangle, AD=AE, and ∠DAE=60°. Therefore AB=AE, and triangle ABE is an isosceles triangle. Also because the equilateral triangle is on the outside of AD, ∠BAE=∠BAD+∠DAE=90°+60°=150°. Thus in triangle ABE the two base angles are equal, ∠ABE=∠AEB=(180°−150°)/2=15°.

method.method_draft: Use direct angle chasing and an isosceles triangle. From the image, identify square ABCD with A at the upper right, B at the upper left, D at the lower right, and the equilateral triangle ADE built outward to the right on side AD; segment BE is drawn and the target angle is at E between EA and EB. From the text, use that ABCD is a square and ADE is equilateral. Thus AB = AD and AD = AE, so AB = AE. Also, at A the square angle between AB and AD is 90 degrees, and the equilateral angle between AD and AE is 60 degrees on the exterior side, so angle BAE = 90 + 60 = 150 degrees. In triangle ABE, sides AB and AE are equal, so the base angles at B and E are equal. Therefore angle AEB = (180 - 150)/2 = 15 degrees.
